clauses.clause: para. 1: creates a three-member emergency board, appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; members must be disinterested
para. 2: board shall report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order
para. 3: no change in the conditions of the dispute, except by agreement, from the order date until thirty days after the board's report

gaps.what: Date the emergency board reported to the President. It would fix an earlier own-terms end of the status quo clause (report plus 30 days) and so the true first end. It does not affect operative status at the cutoff.
gaps.where_to_look: National Mediation Board emergency board reports for 1950 (Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway / Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen); NMB annual report for fiscal 1950; Truman Library

propositions.claim: EO 10125 was printed in the Federal Register of 28 April 1950 at 15 FR 2391 and is dated 26 April 1950.
The order creates a three-member emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act.
propositions.quote: I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute.

propositions.claim: The board must report within thirty days of the order.
propositions.quote: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.

propositions.claim: The order imposes a status quo period running until thirty days after the board's report.
propositions.quote: from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made

propositions.claim: EO 12553 of 25 February 1986 (51 FR 7237) revokes the orders it lists and any amendments to them.
propositions.quote: it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:

propositions.claim: EO 12553's list names EO 10125 by number.
propositions.quote: 10125 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute

propositions.claim: EO 12553 states its purpose as removing orders no longer necessary, which is consistent with the board's work having finished earlier but does not date that.
propositions.quote: to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary

review.conclusion_reason: EO 12553 expressly names and revokes EO 10125 without qualification. This supports NO operative status at October 14, 2026 and formal revocation, with every clause ended no later than February 25, 1986. The result appropriately leaves any earlier report-dependent ending undated.
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed: WEB fits the first gap because the evidence slice supplies the original and express revocation but no evidence of when the board actually reported. The identified NMB or Truman Library records would be needed to resolve that earlier ending; the gap prevents T5.

verdicts.reason: Held official-printing OCR shows EXECUTIVE ORDER 10125, the April 28, 1950 issue heading, page 2391, and the displaced White House signature date April 26, 1950.

Held EO_10125.txt invokes section 10 of the Railway Labor Act and states 'I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate the said dispute.' It also confirms the disinterested-members requirement.
Held EO_10125.txt requires reporting findings 'within thirty days from the date of this order.' This is a reporting deadline, not an automatic termination.
Held EO_10125.txt prohibits changes except by agreement 'from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President.' Actual reporting is required to date this expiry.
Held EO_12553.txt, 51 FR 7237, identifies February 25, 1986 and provides that 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked'.
Held EO_12553.txt at 51 FR 7238 explicitly lists '10125 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'.

The revocation preamble says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary'. Earlier completion is merely consistent with this statement; the statement does not establish completion or its date.
